features: LOAD THE FILE, THE FORM FILLS ITSELF — A supplier invoice no longer has to be typed: pick the XML file the supplier sent by certified email or that you downloaded from the tax portal, and number, dates, amounts, lines, IBAN and supplier fill themselves in. Several documents can be loaded at once: the system reads them all, lists them with supplier, date and amount, and after each save offers the ones still waiting. It accepts plain XML and signed .p7m envelopes.

THE SUPPLIER IS CREATED FROM THE FILE, WITHOUT LEAVING THE PAGE — If the supplier is not on file yet, a button creates it by reading company name, VAT number, address and certified email from the document, and attaches it to the invoice being registered. Before, you had to abandon a half-entered amount and start over. When the file declares a withholding tax and the figures add up, the regime is proposed too — proposed, not decided: the tick can be cleared and the regime changed before saving.

THE PROFESSIONAL FUND CONTRIBUTION NOW REACHES THE INVOICE — On a professional's invoice the 4 or 5% fund contribution was not being recorded: on a real invoice that meant € 3,904.00 instead of € 4,099.20 — € 195.20 missing, with nothing flagging it. It is now an expense line with its own VAT rate, and whether that contribution is subject to withholding tax is read from the document rather than inferred.

THE FILE'S WITHHOLDING TAX COMPARED WITH THE FORM'S — If the document declares a withholding tax and the supplier on file is not marked as subject to one, no screen used to say the two disagreed: the invoice was recorded at the full amount and the building paid nothing to the tax office, while remaining liable for it. The two figures now sit one under the other, with why they differ and what to do. It warns, it does not block: the administrator has the last word. It works both ways round, and when there is nothing to say, nothing appears.

A SOCIAL SECURITY CONTRIBUTION IS NOT A WITHHOLDING TAX — The e-invoice schema uses the same block for six different things: two are withholding taxes, the other four are social security contributions the supplier pays to their own fund, not the building. They are now told apart, and if the file declares one it is reported separately.

A FILE ADDRESSED TO ANOTHER BUILDING DOES NOT GET IN — If the recipient's tax code written in the document is not the one of the building you have open, the file is refused, saying who it is addressed to. If instead it is the building that has no tax code on file, the reader flags it with a link to fix it: it warns without blocking.

WORK TYPED BY HAND IS NO LONGER LOST — Loading an XML onto a form you have already filled in now asks for confirmation first. Before, hand-typed lines — budget items, properties for private works, unbudgeted flags — vanished in one go with no warning.

SMALLER THINGS, ALL FOUND IN USE — Purely descriptive € 0.00 lines no longer demand a budget item. Deleting one line no longer makes another line's error disappear. An unreadable file now says what to do instead of quoting the XML reader's technical text. Registering another document no longer leaves a red message about a file you discarded earlier. And closing the reader while it is still reading no longer lets the document take over the form behind your back.
